## Classes

### <a name="zettarepl"></a>`zettarepl`

This class installs the zettarepl package, manages the zettarepl service and
creates zettarepl_* resources for the global settings, periodic snapshot
tasks, replication tasks and transports in the zettarepl definition file.

#### Examples

##### Hourly snapshots of a dataset replicated to a remote host

```puppet
class { 'zettarepl':
  settings                => {
    'timezone' => 'Europe/Berlin',
  },
  periodic_snapshot_tasks => {
    'data_hourly' => {
      'config' => {
        'dataset'       => 'tank/data',
        'recursive'     => true,
        'lifetime'      => 'P14D',
        'naming-schema' => 'auto-%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M',
        'schedule'      => {
          'minute' => '0',
        },
      },
    },
  },
  transports              => {
    'backup_host' => {
      'config' => {
        'type'        => 'ssh',
        'hostname'    => 'backup.example.com',
        'username'    => 'root',
        'private-key' => $private_key,
        'host-key'    => 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA...',
      },
    },
  },
  replication_tasks       => {
    'data_offsite' => {
      'config' => {
        'direction'               => 'push',
        'transport'               => 'backup_host',
        'source-dataset'          => ['tank/data'],
        'target-dataset'          => 'backup/data',
        'recursive'               => true,
        'periodic-snapshot-tasks' => ['data_hourly'],
        'auto'                    => true,
        'retention-policy'        => 'source',
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Data type: `String[1]`

Overwrite the package `ensure` parameter.

Data type: `Boolean`

##### <a name="-zettarepl--package_name"></a>`package_name`

##### <a name="-zettarepl--periodic_snapshot_tasks"></a>`periodic_snapshot_tasks`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of periodic snapshot tasks to manage.
Each key is the task name. Each value is a hash with:
  - ensure [String] 'present' or 'absent' (default: 'present')
  - config [Hash] Task definition passed to zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--purge"></a>`purge`

Data type: `Boolean`

Set to `true` to remove all periodic snapshot tasks, replication tasks
and transports that are not managed by Puppet.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--replication_tasks"></a>`replication_tasks`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of replication tasks to manage.
Each key is the task name. Each value is a hash with:
  - ensure [String] 'present' or 'absent' (default: 'present')
  - config [Hash] Task definition passed to zettarepl_replication_task.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--service_enable"></a>`service_enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the zettarepl service should be enabled at boot.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--service_ensure"></a>`service_ensure`

Data type: `Enum['running','stopped']`

Whether the zettarepl service should be running.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--service_manage"></a>`service_manage`

Data type: `Boolean`

Set to `false` to disable service management.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--service_name"></a>`service_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

The name of the zettarepl service.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--settings"></a>`settings`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of global zettarepl settings (all top-level keys except the task and
transport sections), e.g. `timezone`. Passed to zettarepl_settings.

##### <a name="-zettarepl--transports"></a>`transports`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of named transports to manage.
Each key is the transport name. Each value is a hash with:
  - ensure [String] 'present' or 'absent' (default: 'present')
  - config [Hash] Transport definition passed to zettarepl_transport.

## Resource types

### <a name="zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task"></a>`zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task`

The task is stored in the `periodic-snapshot-tasks` section of
/usr/local/etc/zettarepl.yaml. The `config` hash is written as-is and
replaces the whole task definition. Validation is performed by zettarepl,
not by Puppet.

#### Examples

##### Take hourly snapshots of a dataset

```puppet
zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task { 'data_hourly':
  ensure => present,
  config => {
    'dataset'       => 'tank/data',
    'recursive'     => true,
    'lifetime'      => 'P14D',
    'naming-schema' => 'auto-%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M',
    'schedule'      => {
      'minute' => '0',
    },
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task` type.

##### `config`

A hash with the complete task definition, using the keys of the
zettarepl `periodic-snapshot-tasks` section (e.g. `dataset`,
`recursive`, `naming-schema`, `schedule`).

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the periodic snapshot task should be present or absent.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task` type.

* [`name`](#-zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task--name)
* [`provider`](#-zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task--provider)

##### <a name="-zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the periodic snapshot task.

##### <a name="-zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `zettarepl_periodic_snapshot_task` resource. You will seldom need to specify this
--- Puppet will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="zettarepl_replication_task"></a>`zettarepl_replication_task`

The task is stored in the `replication-tasks` section of
/usr/local/etc/zettarepl.yaml. The `config` hash is written as-is and
replaces the whole task definition. Validation is performed by zettarepl,
not by Puppet.

#### Examples

##### Push snapshots to a remote host using a named transport

```puppet
zettarepl_replication_task { 'data_offsite':
  ensure => present,
  config => {
    'direction'               => 'push',
    'transport'               => 'backup_host',
    'source-dataset'          => ['tank/data'],
    'target-dataset'          => 'backup/data',
    'recursive'               => true,
    'periodic-snapshot-tasks' => ['data_hourly'],
    'auto'                    => true,
    'retention-policy'        => 'source',
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `zettarepl_replication_task` type.

##### `config`

A hash with the complete task definition, using the keys of the
zettarepl `replication-tasks` section (e.g. `direction`, `transport`,
`source-dataset`, `target-dataset`, `retention-policy`).

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the replication task should be present or absent.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `zettarepl_replication_task` type.

* [`name`](#-zettarepl_replication_task--name)
* [`provider`](#-zettarepl_replication_task--provider)

##### <a name="-zettarepl_replication_task--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the replication task.

##### <a name="-zettarepl_replication_task--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `zettarepl_replication_task` resource. You will seldom need to specify this ---
Puppet will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="zettarepl_settings"></a>`zettarepl_settings`

Global settings are all top-level keys of /usr/local/etc/zettarepl.yaml
except the `periodic-snapshot-tasks`, `replication-tasks` and `transports`
sections. The `config` hash replaces all global settings, so keys missing
from `config` are removed. Only one instance of this type should be
declared. Validation is performed by zettarepl, not by Puppet.

#### Examples

##### Set the timezone and limit parallel replication tasks

```puppet
zettarepl_settings { 'zettarepl':
  config => {
    'max-parallel-replication-tasks' => 2,
    'timezone'                       => 'Europe/Berlin',
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `zettarepl_settings` type.

##### `config`

A hash with all global settings, using the top-level keys of the
zettarepl definition file (e.g. `timezone`,
`max-parallel-replication-tasks`, `use-removal-dates`).

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `zettarepl_settings` type.

* [`name`](#-zettarepl_settings--name)
* [`provider`](#-zettarepl_settings--provider)

##### <a name="-zettarepl_settings--name"></a>`name`

namevar

An arbitrary name for this resource, usually `zettarepl`.

##### <a name="-zettarepl_settings--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `zettarepl_settings` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will
usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="zettarepl_transport"></a>`zettarepl_transport`

The transport is stored in the `transports` section of
/usr/local/etc/zettarepl.yaml and can be referenced by name in the
`transport` key of replication tasks. The `config` hash is written as-is
and replaces the whole transport definition. Validation is performed by
zettarepl, not by Puppet.

The `config` property is always treated as sensitive, because SSH
transports contain a private key.

#### Examples

##### Define an SSH transport

```puppet
zettarepl_transport { 'backup_host':
  ensure => present,
  config => {
    'type'        => 'ssh',
    'hostname'    => 'backup.example.com',
    'username'    => 'root',
    'private-key' => $private_key,
    'host-key'    => 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA...',
  },
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `zettarepl_transport` type.

##### `config`

A hash with the complete transport definition, using the keys of the
zettarepl `transports` section (e.g. `type`, `hostname`, `username`,
`private-key`, `host-key`).

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the transport should be present or absent.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `zettarepl_transport` type.

* [`name`](#-zettarepl_transport--name)
* [`provider`](#-zettarepl_transport--provider)

##### <a name="-zettarepl_transport--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the transport.

##### <a name="-zettarepl_transport--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `zettarepl_transport` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet
will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.
